conceptual assets.information: The run-time setting enables the serial link and controls whether the RX and TX FIFOs are cleared and interrupts are active; link operation depends on it.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because a bus write changes the setting at line 148, allowing an unauthorized modification of link behavior. Availability is at risk because the setting clears both FIFOs when disabled at lines 226 and 294 and gates interrupt generation at lines 259 and 310.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write could clear queued data and disable link servicing by clearing the enable setting.

conceptual assets.information: The setting selects the destination identifier inserted into transmitted link words; correct routing of transmitted packets depends on it.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because a bus write changes the stored destination at line 161 and the value is inserted into transmitted FIFO words at line 296, determining the destination output at line 300.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write could redirect transmitted packets to an unintended destination.

conceptual assets.information: The receive-side valid and ready protocol determines whether words are accepted from the serial link; RX transfers depend on this handshake.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the incoming valid signal is used as the RX FIFO write strobe at line 229 and the ready signal is driven from FIFO capacity at line 233, so either can produce an incorrect transfer decision. Availability is at risk because holding the ready or valid handshake inactive prevents RX words from moving.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress the ready response or corrupt the valid indication to drop or stall received transfers.

conceptual assets.information: The transmit-side valid and ready protocol determines whether queued words move to the serial link; TX transfers depend on this handshake.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the peer ready signal directly controls FIFO reads at line 298 and the valid output is generated from FIFO availability at line 302, so either can cause an incorrect transfer decision. Availability is at risk because holding ready or valid inactive blocks transmission of queued words.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the ready input or valid output inactive to stall transmission or cause a word to be consumed at the wrong time.

conceptual assets.information: The RX interrupt indicates configured receive-FIFO occupancy conditions; system software depends on it to service received data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the RX interrupt output is produced from enable, threshold settings and FIFO status at lines 259 through 262, allowing a false or missing event. Availability is at risk because suppressing the event can prevent software from servicing the receive FIFO and eventually stall reception.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress or forge the RX interrupt so received data is not serviced or software reacts incorrectly.

conceptual assets.information: The TX interrupt indicates configured transmit-FIFO occupancy conditions; system software depends on it to provide or manage transmitted data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the TX interrupt output is produced from enable, threshold settings and FIFO status at lines 310 through 313, allowing a false or missing event. Availability is at risk because suppressing the event can prevent software from replenishing or managing the transmit FIFO and stall transmission.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress or forge the TX interrupt so software fails to replenish the FIFO or performs an incorrect service operation.

The source field is only copied from the FIFO read word into a read-back register and returned, so Port buffers treats the register as a movement-only copy rather than an independent asset (lines 189, 248).

The packet-last field is only copied from the FIFO read word into a read-back register and returned, so Port buffers treats the register as a movement-only copy rather than an independent asset (lines 169, 245).

The bus data and packet marker are relayed through the TX FIFO to the serial output without this unit storing or computing the payload, so Forwarded transactions and Port buffers bar a separate conceptual asset (lines 296, 299, 301).

FIFO availability, free-space and half-full values are buffer flags and their bus read-back bits, which Port buffers and Buffer and engine status bits treat as properties of buffered transfers rather than independent information (lines 171 through 176, 214, 219, 282, 287).

considered, not kept.reason: The clear controls only clear FIFO buffers through rx_fifo.clear and tx_fifo.clear, so Port buffers bars them as independent pieces except for the separately retained link-enable setting (lines 149, 150, 226, 294).

These bus-written settings only tune the interrupt outputs, so Port options treats them as configuration of those outputs rather than concepts of their own (lines 152 through 157, 259 through 262, 310 through 313).

The acknowledge repeats the request strobe and the error is constant, so Bus handshake copies bars an independent response-status concept (lines 135 and 136).
